evidence_quotes.agenda: 'Do you have any questions or concerns in regards to this move specifically?' — asked immediately after intro, before any logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer asked to compare weekend vs. weekday rates; rep pulled both actual numbers (Sunday $192/hr vs Tuesday $190/hr), and followed through to actually rebooking the move for Tuesday the 8th.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: 'I would estimate between 6:00 and seven just with elevators and four [floors]' plus 'once we go over that minimum the time is per rated in fifteen minute increments.'

top_strength: Full differentiator delivery — damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, AND the day-before/on-the-way communication calls were all covered clearly, and the rep actually pulled live pricing to answer a real comparison question.
coaching_note: Save Your Ass is still missing its strongest closer-quality lines (no experience/commit-to-rate framing, no self-prep tip, no 'does that feel fair' pause) — worth layering in even on an already-booked confirmation call to build extra confidence before the move.
grading_notes: Judgment call: stage3_close scored full credit (5) since this is an auto-booking-online confirmation call — the customer was already committed and the call's real 'close' moment was rebooking to a different day, which the rep executed cleanly; no natural rate-lock/explicit-ask line was needed.
